newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Livent plans Dr. Seuss musical.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Livent plans Dr. Seuss musical.

text.p: Canadian theatrical producer Livent Inc. said on Tuesday it has acquired rights to the classic children's stories of Dr. Seuss and planned to develop a Broadway musical called "The Seussical" in 1999.

Toronto-based Livent said the musical would feature Seuss's 1957 landmark "Cat in the Hat" and include other famous Seuss characters such as Horton from "Horton Hears a Who" and the Grinch from "How the Grinch Stole Christmas".
Livent, which produced such Tony award-winning musicals as "Kiss of the Spider Woman" and "Showboat," said it hired Ken Ludwig to turn the Seuss books into a play.
Ludwig wrote the book for the "Crazy for You" and "Lend Me a Tenor" plays.
Livent Chief Executive Garth Drabinsky said Ludwig was chosen for his humour and his ability to relate to the stories.

"First of all, he has a very good sense of structure when he writes, but most importantly he is a very funny writer and he has a couple of young kids so he really understands the material," Drabinsky said.
He said the composer and lyricist would be chosen later.
Drabinsky would not estimate the costs of creating "The Seussical." Livent's current theatrical production of "Ragtime" cost C$8 million ($5.7 million) to produce.
Livent also did not disclose what it paid for the rights to the Seuss books by the late Theodor Geisel. But Drabinsky said the negotiations for the books were "brief."
Geisel, one of the most popular and innovative children's writers, was born in 1904 and wrote 44 popular children's books under the pen name of Dr. Seuss before his death in 1991.
Many of his stories were made into television cartoons and timeless holiday specials. He won two Academy Awards and a Pulitzer prize in 1984.
Livent spokeswoman Eleanor Goldhar said the Seuss play would open at one of Livent's theatres in Toronto, Vancouver, New York and Chicago.
